source.citation: Unidentified author, article on nervous and reflex cough, Medical Record 56 (August 5, 1899): 189–190. Author and title to confirm from the page image.

complaints: a persistent hacking cough at regular intervals, lasting a few seconds
presentation.priorTreatment: Remedies of various kinds, without effect.

findings: no physical signs, no expectoration, no constitutional symptoms
several competent examiners found nothing in the respiratory tract
an occasional, inconstant bruit below the left collarbone; no sign of aneurism
periodDiagnosis: nervous cough of central origin (possibly anaemic)
outcome: Unresolved; the author admits the cause was not clear.
quotes: If not a neurosis, I have so far failed to find the cause.

modernReading.text: Probably a habit cough or vocal tic. Anaemia, which the author suggests, would not explain it. Long hours in a dusty sweatshop are worth asking about.

fixed: regular hacking cough with no chest findings

constrained.rule: needle trades or similar indoor work
sponsored or comfortable; wages matter to the family

notes: One of very few cards so far with a named immigrant group. The author's uncertainty is part of the case.
